citation.author: Ventomäki, Hanna
citation.title: Representation of nature in Red Dead Redemption 2
citation.type: MA thesis (University of Oulu, English / Language and Literature)

discipline: English literary studies / ecocriticism / game studies
thesis: RDR2 represents nature and civilization as separate, opposed entities (civilization overcoming nature through industrialization, mirroring the late-19th-century US); nature is coded with respite/freedom/frontier-spirit/survival while industrial space is restrictive/polluted/inhospitable, and this opposition is built across spatial narratives, mechanics, and Western-genre themes — but nature is simultaneously Romanticized, exploited, antagonistic, and autonomous, an irreducibly multifaceted set of representations co-authored by player choice.
sections: 1. Introduction (three research questions: dynamic nature-spaces, Western themes, in-game construction)
2. Literature review (nature-in-videogames; environmentalism/conservation; exergames; anthropocentrism; biophilia/landscape preference; Western genre; nature-in-Westerns)
3. Analytical framework (3.1 realism/space; 3.1.1 spatial narrative; 3.2 contemporary Western themes; 3.3 multimodality; 3.4 subjective/objective experience)
4. Description of materials and methods (single-analyst close reading of six chapters; Arthur arc; screenshots/fair use)

5. Analysis (5.1 physical spaces; 5.1.1 New Austin vs Annesburg; 5.2 maps/journal; 5.3 hunting/survival; 5.4 animals; 5.5 Western-theme narratives; 5.5.1 loading screens; 5.5.2 Old West narratives in nature/space; 5.6 close analysis 'Exit Pursued by a Bruised Ego')
6. Discussion (nature-culture as separable opposites; Arthur as Old West embodiment; New West victory via his death)
7. Conclusion (mainly Romantic nature as mirror to authentic self; conservation messaging vs. elective exploitation)
concepts: nature representation as multimodal construction (Elleström's four modalities)
spatial narrative / environmental storytelling (evocative spaces, embedded narratives, cause-and-effect)
nature defined as the uncontrolled (Öhman et al.)
anthropocentrism and the eco-conundrum (eco-content in an exploitative medium)
Old West / New West frontier nostalgia
Romanticism of nature (mirror to authentic self)
revisionist Western critique of the industrial-capitalist present
autonomy of nature (animals acting independently of the player)
readings: New Austin vs. Annesburg: gated desert (Old West, John-only) vs. polluted coal town (New West) as authored nature-culture commentary
Maps and Arthur's journal as humanizing meta-narrative; journal's nature-over-culture bias characterizes Arthur
Hunting ethics: contests Saxton Brown — methodical clean kill as humane/conservationist; exploitation is contextual
Bison/poacher mission (Charles Smith): positions player on side of nature/conservation; bison near-extinction + indigenous colonization
Honor mechanic as ecological feedback (care=honor, excess=dishonor; buck vs. black coyote endings; 'Manifest Destiny' counter-pole)
Horses (revisionist via McMahon/Tompkins): marginalized emotional parallel; controllable link to nature; taming white Arabian as conquest
Loading-screen photographs: wistful frontier nostalgia; bird-on-stump read ambivalently (decline vs. reclamation)
'The New South' fishing trip: 'last good moments before the fall'; sunset as decline-symbol
Campsites as barometer: six sites trending toward industrialized areas; Beaver Hollow near Annesburg pollution

Close analysis 'Exit Pursued by a Bruised Ego': bear hunt with Hosea; cinematic city-to-wild transition; unsettling skinning + meat-industry reflection; antagonized scarred bear; asymmetry of man over nature

game_elements.how_treated: Ambarino (snow/glaciers/Grizzlies), New Hanover (plains/forests/Annesburg), Lemoyne (meadows/Bayou Nwa/Saint Denis), West Elizabeth (Blackwater/Strawberry/Arabian snowfields), New Austin (arid SW desert, gated for Arthur), Guarma (restricted tropical island) — each a real-US analog establishing nature-culture geography
iconic Old West arid landscape locked off during Arthur playthrough, reserved for John in epilogue; inaccessibility read as commentary on disappearing Old West
black smoke, oil/garbage-polluted water, dead fish, sickly population, hostile mine guards, no stable; embodies industrialization's cost to environment and people
'curse' revealed as lead/arsenic mine poisoning; lumber camp clear-cuts then is abandoned — capitalist exploitation of nature

binocular 1-3 star quality rating, Eagle Eye tracking (wind/tracks/clues), correct-caliber clean kill, skinning + carcass harvest, pelts to satchels/garments/talismans, predator bait; read as partly humane/conservationist, contesting blanket-exploitation view
indigenous conservation ethic ('move with the bison'), admiration, slaughtered-herd discovery; positions player on side of nature/conservation; comments on bison near-extinction and colonization
conservation/animal-care rewarded with honor, excess killing penalized with dishonor; ending and self-image keyed to honor (buck vs. black coyote); never prohibits killing
given personalities/reputations/emotional ties; interact autonomously (hawks fishing, birds on bison); compendium situates ecology

game_elements.element: Horses (white Arabian, war horses, abused mounts)
game_elements.how_treated: main transport; bonding (ride/feed/groom) and customization; revisionist reading — marginalized emotional parallel, controllable link to nature; taming Arabian as conquest/mastery
nature's deadliness personified; man-vs-nature adversary; legendary panther mythified by NPC tales; antagonized (alligator red eyes); some gated behind prior hunting achievements
cold-rain shivering, warmth-rated clothing vs. draining health core, location-specific events (New Austin dust storms, glacier extremes); 48-min day; ties player tangibly to world
hand-drawn markers and private journal humanize interface, grant privileged interior access; nature-over-culture sketch bias characterizes Arthur; distinct Arthur/John handwriting
habitat, hunting method, kill-count, uses; multimodally communicates the game-world's ecology
12 sepia stills (collapsed cottage, snowy Grizzlies, pioneer, bird-on-stump) set wistful Old West nostalgia; ambivalent decline-vs-reclamation symbolism

game_elements.element: Campsites (six, incl. Horseshoe Overlook, Beaver Hollow)
game_elements.how_treated: barometer of gang wellbeing; trend toward industrialized areas as nature recedes; Horseshoe = Old West ideal, Beaver Hollow = decline near Annesburg pollution
mirror-clear lake at sunset, singing; 'last good moments before the fall'; sunset as decline-symbol

game_elements.element: 'Exit Pursued by a Bruised Ego' (legendary Bharati bear)
game_elements.how_treated: tutorialized saddle-switch in narrative; cinematic city-to-wild transition (human insignificance); realistic skinning prompting meat-industry reflection; Dead Eye combat; scarred antagonized bear; man-over-nature asymmetry (Arthur heals, bear dies)

game_elements.element: Conservation-vector NPCs (Charles Smith, Malcolm MacIntosh, Mary-Beth, Hosea, Dutch)
game_elements.how_treated: Charles=indigenous conservation; MacIntosh=anti-mining scientist selling 'Hopes for the Future'; Mary-Beth=Arthur's needless-killing confession; Hosea=hunting mentor; Dutch=Old-West-freedom ideology

themes: nature vs. civilization as separable opposites
frontier nostalgia and the decline of the Old West (Arthur's death = New West victory)
man-vs-nature as the simplest pre-political struggle
nature as safe space / authentic selfhood (Romanticism)
player agency and moral ambiguity (hunting freedom vs. conservation messaging)

Saxton Brown (2014) — anthropocentrism, eco-conundrum, hunting-as-exploitation (partly contested)

McVeigh (2007) — post-9/11 Western re-emergence, political anxiety
Walsh (2016) — John Ford's mythic West, Monument Valley
McFarlane (2019) — nature in Westerns (beauty/doom/neutral); universality of themes
Domsch (2019) — space/narrative in computer games; spatial-narrative taxonomy
McMahon (2010) — revisionist horses in the Western
Tompkins (1992) — horses as unseen symbolic labor; man-nature link
Balakrishnan & Sundar (2011); Hassan (2020); Lastowka & Ogino (2014) — navigation/immersion, graphics, screenshot fair-use

debate_axis_positions.position: Net lean toward aesthetic/ecological (Romantic nature, conservation valorized, exploitation displaced onto antagonists), but explicitly reframes the axis as both/and-in-tension rather than either/or; player choice co-determines which pole dominates.
debate_axis_positions.evidence: hunting/pelt-economy = resource pole (per Saxton Brown), contested by survival-hunting-as-natural, humane clean kill, conservation mission, MacIntosh protest, honor feedback, animal autonomy, journal, loading screens

debate_axis_positions.position: Holds both: mechanic is exploitative in itself, framed as survival-necessary, condemned in excess via Charles/Mary-Beth, yet never prohibited.
Reads RDR2 as predominantly nostalgic/Romantic (Old West idealized) while registering revisionist currents (horses, industrial critique).
debate_axis_positions.evidence: Carter, McVeigh; horse section conceded one-sidedly revisionist

tensions: conservation message vs. unbounded killing (commentary and player freedom collide)
hunting as exploitative vs. necessary (contextual: food vs. trophy)
Romanticized vs. exploited nature; antagonist vs. autonomous nature
single-analyst subjectivity (acknowledged; horse section one-sidedly revisionist)
protagonist-dependence of the nature-culture juxtaposition (raised, left open)
